_about: Bridge (Track WS, 2026-10-10: water). ALEX'S (decisions water-layer and bridge-look): a bridge where the village road crosses the river, 'destroyable like the radio tower' (the lead's proposal; Alex: 'Sounds good'), the stone arch with a flat deck. EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track WS. A STATIC unit (mobility 'static', like the radio tower and the batteries): it never moves, turns or plans, has no weapons, and goes down with the fate 'destroyed' when its health reaches 0, so bombs can bring it down (the World judges it like any ground unit: bombs.json's blast hurts a unit at the surface). It is a bomb target in principle and NO PART OF THE STRIKE'S MISSION (the mission names the radio tower and the bomber only). It stands at the road's crossing of the river (WaterGen.sites().bridge, scenario site 'water.bridge') with the road's heading. Domain ground: a structure on the surface band (a boat sails under it; the drawing draws it, data/world/bridges.json).

size_m._reason: the span over the river (26 m at the road: Alex, decision water-layer, river_width) plus an abutment of 6 m on each bank (data/world/bridges.json abutment_len_m): about 38 m along the road, rounded to 40; the deck is 16 m wide

draught_m._reason: a bridge does not float: only a sea unit needs water under it

actions_per_turn._reason: a static unit has nothing to plan: one step a turn that stands still

health._reason: ALEX (decision bridge-durability, 2026-10-11), asked whether tank guns may damage a bridge: 'it should take a lot. Like you would have to sit there and shell it for awhile exposing yourself.' So a tank's gun CAN bring a bridge down (1 pip a hit), and it takes a long, exposed time. THE NUMBER 14 IS PROPOSED (Track CA; was 10, the bombs' figure). MEASURED with the real combat (scripts/test_support/bridge_tuning.gd, 120 seeds): one tank's turret gun, stationary anywhere inside its 350 m effective range, takes 0.73 pips a turn, so 14 pips is a MEDIAN OF 20 TURNS of steady fire (10th to 90th percentile 13 to 23; the old 10 pips was 14 [10..17]) -- 100 seconds sitting within 350 m of the bridge, in sight and in range of whatever defends it. The lead's proposed target was about 15 to 20 turns. WHAT IT DOES TO THE REST (the same script): BOMBS (3 / 2 / 1 pips at 12 / 25 / 45 m, a stick of 4, a load of 3 sticks): no single stick can do it (the most is 12), a bomber at the LOW band on the ideal release needs 2 sticks (mean 2.1), at medium 3 to 4 (3.4: a whole load, if every stick is good), at high 9; THE CRUISER (6 shells of 4 / 3 / 2 pips at 6 / 12 / 20 m, data/sim/guns.json): a FRESH direct salvo cannot (the most it did in 400 seeds was 13 pips at 1200 m, 7 at 3000 m), one ranged in for 10 s cannot either bar 1 percent, one ranged in for the full 20 s does it 35 percent of the time at 1200 m (1 percent at 3000 m), the next one, with a salvo already on the bridge, 81 percent (7 percent at 3000 m), the one after 99 percent (43 percent at 3000 m): a bridge shelled by guns that have found their range goes in two or three salvos. Only 25 pips or more would be proof against a fully ranged salvo (the most 6 shells can do is 24), and that is 34 turns for a tank and nearly a full load for a low bomber

shape._about: THE LOW BRIDGE (Alex, decision line-of-fire: '(c) A low bridge: the deck level with the banks, with 1 m parapets, and the drawing's shadow lowered to match.'). Three boxes, all stamped into the height grid while the bridge stands: the DECK, level with the banks (the banks and the water's surface are 0 m in the grid, so the deck's top is 0 and a tank on it stands at 0 m) -- standable, and no target (data/sim/line_of_fire.json targets.not_targets names 'deck': a level surface has nothing to hit) -- and two PARAPETS, 1 m of stone along the deck's two sides, which are what a line of fire meets and what the bridge is as a target. The deck's top is data/world/bridges.json arch.crown_h and the parapets' height arch.parapet_h; test_line_of_fire_combat holds both equal. The arches under the deck are not modelled (2.5D has one top height per cell). The box positions and sizes are PROPOSED by builder LOF2 from the drawing (deck_width_m 16, parapet_w 1 to 1.2, the unit's 40 m); the heights are Alex's.
